text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick on Tuesday criticised attempts by Germany's coalition government to reform its Budget programme as being "one-sided".
"The savings which have been made so far seem to me to be very one-sided," Koebnick told German radio.
Koebnick, also president of the state central bank in the Rhineland-Palatinate and Saar regions, said virtually no cuts were being made in the agriculture area.
Savings need to be "of the right amount and in all the right places," Koebnick warned.

From the banking point of view, the main issue was keeping the budgetary deficit below three percent, working towards achieving a budget surplus as quickly as possible and reducing government debt, Koepnick said.

Koepnick said he supported a stability package for currency union, which was in the interest of all states which were interested in taking part in monetary union. This includes using sanctions to keep countries on the path to convergence.
"If levels of new debts hit a particular level, then any sanctions have to come in automatically," Koepnick said.
The introduction of a stability pact required a longer consultation period. "If agreement is reached by the summer, that will be time enough," said Koepnick.
